fixes.explanation: Jacob never mentions flocks here, friend. What he tells his household is, “Get rid of the foreign gods that are among you.” Sheep don't show up anywhere in that sentence. The gods are what he names.

Tents don't come up in Jacob's words, friend. He tells his household and all who were with him, “Get rid of the foreign gods that are among you.” That's the item on his list. The verse leaves the tents out of it.

Yes, friend. Jacob says, “Purify yourselves and change your garments.” Then he says they will go to Bethel, where he will build an altar to God. Whenever I put on a clean apron, I stand up a little straighter myself.
No haircuts on this list, friend. Jacob's words are, “Purify yourselves and change your garments.” So the other instruction is about clothes. Heads never come up.
That's it, friend. The verse says they gave Jacob “all their foreign gods and all their earrings.” Notice the word all shows up twice in that one line. That's a lot of all for one verse.
Sandals aren't in this verse, friend. The household gives Jacob “all their foreign gods and all their earrings.” Earrings is the word that fills the blank. Footwear never comes up.
Staffs get no mention in this verse, friend. The text says they gave Jacob “all their foreign gods and all their earrings.” Foreign gods and earrings are the list it gives. Earrings is your blank.
True, friend. The text says, “Jacob buried them under the oak near Shechem.” The "them" is the foreign gods and the earrings the household had just handed over. So both of them go under that oak.
Yes, friend. The text says, “a terror from God fell over the surrounding cities.” It came from God Himself, and it fell on the cities around them. I think that was good news for Jacob's sons.
No storm in this verse, friend. The text says, “a terror from God fell over the surrounding cities.” The word is terror, not storm. What fell on those cities came from God.

It's the other way around, friend. The text says the terror from God fell over the surrounding cities “so that they did not pursue Jacob’s sons.” So the cities did not chase them. That makes this one False.

False is right, friend. The terror from God fell over the surrounding cities “so that they did not pursue Jacob’s sons.” So the cities do not chase them. The statement says they did, and that's why it's False.

Beersheba is a real place name, friend, but it's not the one here. The text says, “There Jacob built an altar, and he called that place El-bethel…” So Jacob builds the altar and names the place El-bethel. He's in Luz, which is also called Bethel.

Prophets are a fair guess, friend, but that's not the word God uses. He says, “A nation—even a company of nations—shall come from you, and kings shall descend from you.” The word in the verse is kings. That's a whole lot of future to hand one man in one breath.

Priests would be a good guess, friend, but God doesn't say that here. His words are, “A nation—even a company of nations—shall come from you, and kings shall descend from you.” He starts with a nation, stretches it to a company of nations, then adds kings. That promise gets bigger with every phrase.

Right, friend. God says, “The land that I gave to Abraham and Isaac I will give to you…” Abraham is Isaac's father (Genesis 25:19). So God names both of them as the ones He gave the land to, and says He will give it to Jacob and to his descendants after him.

Noah is a great name, friend, but he's not in this verse. God says, “The land that I gave to Abraham and Isaac I will give to you…” The name in that line is Abraham, with Isaac right behind him. Then God says the land is for Jacob and his descendants.

Lot's not on the guest list for this one, friend. God says, “The land that I gave to Abraham and Isaac I will give to you…” The blank is Abraham, and Isaac comes right after him. Then God turns to Jacob: the land is for him, and for his descendants after him.

Yes, friend. The text says, “Jacob set up a pillar in the place where God had spoken with him—a stone marker—” and then he pours a drink offering on it and anoints it with oil. So the answer is a stone pillar. I mark my spots with cookie stamps, so a stone marker is a step up.

True, friend. The text says Jacob “poured out a drink offering on it and anointed it with oil.” The "it" is the stone pillar he just set up where God had spoken with him. So the drink offering goes on the pillar, and the oil follows.

That's it, friend. The midwife tells Rachel, “Do not be afraid, for you are having another son.” Rachel is in severe labor, so those words land in a hard moment. I think this is a heavy part of the story.

That's him, friend. The verse says, “Jacob returned to his father Isaac at Mamre, near Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac had stayed.” So Jacob comes back to his father Isaac at Mamre. Hebron is the other name for Kiriath-arba.
